title: Simile or metaphor? Comparing in poems
examples: What is the difference between a simile and a metaphor?
Give me an example of a simile

explain.say: If I say your friend is as brave as a lion, do you picture a lion? Poets love to compare things to make pictures in your mind. Look at the board: the word simile, said in three beats, sim, i, le. Say it with me!

draw.text: Simile or metaphor? Comparing in poems

explain.say: A simile compares two things using like or as. Look at the first group on the board: brave as a lion, ran like the wind, cold as ice. Spot the little words like and as? They are the giveaway. Can you make a simile for the sun?

Now look at the second group: metaphors. A metaphor says something is something else. She is a lion. Of course she is not really a lion, but it shows she is brave, strong and fierce. Can you feel how strong that sounds?
Time is a thief. My room is a zoo. See them in the metaphor box? No like, no as. Just is. Which is messier, a room like a zoo, or a room that is a zoo?

Wonderful! Similes say like or as, metaphors say it is. Wow: we use metaphors every day without noticing, like a heart of gold or a bright idea. Challenge: turn the simile cold as ice into a metaphor.

faq.q: What is the difference between a simile and a metaphor?
faq.a: A simile compares using like or as: brave as a lion. A metaphor says one thing is another: she is a lion.

faq.q: Give me an example of a simile
faq.a: The baby slept like a log. The sea was as smooth as glass. Her smile was like sunshine.
Metaphors make a quick, strong picture and help you feel an idea. Time is a thief makes you feel time being stolen from you.

faq.q: Is a heart of gold a metaphor?
faq.a: Yes. Nobody has a real gold heart; it means a very kind person. Everyday language is full of metaphors like this.
Personification gives human actions to things that are not human, like The wind whispered or The stars danced.

facts: Simile comes from the Latin similis, meaning like or similar.
Metaphor comes from a Greek word meaning to carry across: it carries meaning from one thing to another.
